New #NoisyTCP #vulnerability lets attackers crash #Linux #servers
This pre-authenticated remote corruption flaw (tracked as #CVE-2026-99288) stems from a NULL pointer dereference weakness in the #LinuxKernel's #TCP networking subsystem.
While CVE-2026-99288 exploits cause a #kernelpanic and take down the host, they don't allow threat actors to alter data or gain arbitrary code execution.
https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/linux/new-noisytcp-linux-kernel-flaw-lets-attackers-crash-servers/ #DenialOfService #DOS #ITSec

CVE-2026-99288.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

inet: reject unhashed sockets during established lookups

TCP established ehash lookups are lockless. The socket caches involved
use SLAB_TYPESAFE_BY_RCU, so memory can be reused before an RCU reader
that retained its old address has finished.

After a tuple match, __inet_lookup_established() and
__inet6_lookup_established() acquire a reference and repeat the tuple
check. They do not check whether the new object is hashed. If the
address is reused for a socket with the same tuple, the lookup can
acquire a reference to the new object and return it while its nulls node
is unhashed.

A PoC that drives reuse with a SYN cookie request socket reproduced the
crash. The new request socket is unhashed and has a NULL rsk_listener.
A lookup that had loaded the address of the old request socket acquired
the reference published by tcp_get_cookie_sock() and returned the new
object. tcp_v4_rcv() then read sk_state through the NULL listener.

The resulting crash was:

  BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference, address: 0000000000000012
  #PF: supervisor read access in kernel mode
  #PF: error_code(0x0000) - not-present page
  ...
  Oops: Oops: 0000 [#1] SMP NOPTI
  CPU: 4 UID: 0 PID: 0 Comm: swapper/4 Not tainted 7.3.0-00591-g0e135910deec #1 PREEMPT(lazy)
  ...
  RIP: 0010:tcp_v4_rcv+0x44e/0x1280
  ...
  R10: 0000000000000001 R11: 00000000024ca8c0 R12: 0000000000000000
  ...
  CR2: 0000000000000012 CR3: 0000000103d50004 CR4: 0000000000770ef0
  ...
  Call Trace:
   <IRQ>
   ? raw_local_deliver+0xae/0x240
   ip_protocol_deliver_rcu+0x2d/0x180
   ip_local_deliver_finish+0x84/0x100
   ip_sublist_rcv_finish+0x5f/0x70
   ip_sublist_rcv+0x12a/0x1d0
   ip_list_rcv+0xfd/0x130
   __netif_receive_skb_list_core+0x223/0x250
   netif_receive_skb_list_internal+0x1d2/0x2c0
   ? try_fill_recv+0x39/0x7b0
   napi_complete_done+0x74/0x170
   virtnet_poll+0x445/0x600
   __napi_poll+0x27/0x1e0
   net_rx_action+0x2fe/0x3b0
   handle_softirqs+0xc2/0x2c0
   __irq_exit_rcu+0x74/0xd0
   common_interrupt+0x7f/0x90
   </IRQ>
  ...
  Kernel panic - not syncing: Fatal exception in interrupt

After taking a reference, check whether the nulls node is unhashed in
both IPv4 and IPv6 established lookups. If it is unhashed or the tuple
no longer matches, drop the reference and restart the lookup.

Lookups racing with the TIME_WAIT hashdance, or with a request being
replaced by its child, now restart and find the new socket instead of
returning the old one.

Request sockets that were never inserted into ehash can have a nonzero
refcount, and a stale lookup can hold a transient reference. Therefore,
when SYN cookie, Fast Open, and request migration paths fail after
setting a nonzero refcount, release the references held by those paths
with reqsk_put() instead of freeing the request directly.

CVE-2026-42271.description: LiteLLM is a proxy server (AI Gateway) to call LLM APIs in OpenAI (or native) format. From version 1.74.2 to before version 1.83.7, two endpoints used to preview an MCP server before saving it — POST /mcp-rest/test/connection and POST /mcp-rest/test/tools/list — accepted a full server configuration in the request body, including the command, args, and env fields used by the stdio transport. When called with a stdio configuration, the endpoints attempted to connect, which spawned the supplied command as a subprocess on the proxy host with the privileges of the proxy process. The endpoints were gated only by a valid proxy API key, with no role check. Any authenticated user — including holders of low-privilege internal-user keys — could therefore run arbitrary commands on the host. This issue has been patched in version 1.83.7.

CVE-2026-48710.description: Starlette is a lightweight ASGI framework/toolkit. Prior to version 1.0.1, the HTTP `Host` request header was not validated before being used to reconstruct `request.url`. Because the routing algorithm relies on the raw HTTP path while `request.url` is rebuilt from the `Host` header, a malformed header could make `request.url.path` differ from the path that was actually requested. Middleware and endpoints that apply security restrictions based on `request.url` (rather than the raw `scope` path) could therefore be bypassed. Users should upgrade to a version greater than or equal to version 1.0.1, which validates the `Host` header against the grammar of RFC 9112 §3.2 / RFC 3986 §3.2.2 when constructing `request.url` and falls back to `scope["server"]` for malformed values.

CVE-2026-90436.description:
** UNSUPPORTED WHEN ASSIGNED ** Deserialization of an inbound SOAP fault in Apache Axis 1.x allows unauthenticated remote class instantiation. When a SOAP <Fault> carries a <detail><exceptionName> element, Axis loads the named class and, if a String <data> element is also present, instantiates it through its String constructor before checking that it is an AxisFault. Loading alone runs the class's static initializer. With a suitable class on the application's classpath this leads to remote code execution. The fault is parsed while the engine resolves the target service, before any per-service handler chain runs, so authentication handlers configured on a service do not protect against it. This affects all Apache Axis 1.x versions through 1.4.



As Axis 1 has been EOL we recommend you migrate to a different SOAP engine, such as Apache Axis 2/Java. Apple spends BILLIONS marketing the iPhone as the smartphone that protects your privacy.

"Privacy. That's iPhone."

But what if an app could listen through your microphone AFTER you explicitly denied permission?

🚨 That's the uncomfortable reality behind iOS vulnerability CVE-2026-65339.

The flaw allowed a sandboxed app to forge an audit token trusted by Apple's own audio daemon, audiomxd, potentially bypassing the microphone permission check and capturing real audio.

And the detail that makes this even worse?

The orange microphone indicator could remain OFF.

The recording activity could also escape proper attribution in the relevant system logs.

Apple's privacy messaging tells users they are in control. But a permission prompt means very little if the operating system has a vulnerability that lets an application bypass it.

To be clear, this was a specific local exploit, not proof that Apple was secretly listening to users or that every iPhone was affected.

Still, here's a question for the Apple ecosystem:

If an iPhone can be tricked into recording audio after microphone access was denied, how much confidence should users place in Apple's privacy promises?

We investigated how the exploit worked, how Apple's audio service was fooled, and what the vulnerability reveals about iOS security.

Read the technical breakdown:
https://thecybersecguru.com/exploits/cve-2026-65339-ios-microphone-audit-token-bypass/

Apple's CVE-2026-65339 exposes a disturbing flaw in iOS that allowed a sandboxed app to bypass the microphone permission check and capture real audio without the user's consent.

No jailbreak. No memory corruption. No special entitlements.

Even more concerning, recordings on the vulnerable build were not attributed to the app in the logs, and the orange microphone privacy indicator did not appear.

Apple has patched the vulnerability, but the technical breakdown raises serious questions about how iOS enforces microphone permissions and protects user privacy.

We break down the exploit, the audit token forgery, how the bypass worked and which Apple updates fix it.

#MicrosoftOutlook #NTLM #Cyberveille

🚨 Microsoft Outlook zero-day CVE-2026-124194 is under active exploitation, and CISA has given federal agencies 14 days to patch it.

An attacker sends a crafted Outlook message file (.msg or .oft). When the victim opens it, classic Outlook silently connects to an attacker-controlled server without the usual external-content warning, and Windows sends the user’s NTLMv2 authentication response. The victim types no password and sees no dialog.

The captured response can be cracked offline or used in NTLM relay attacks and Active Directory compromise. It can also feed AD CS ESC8 certificate abuse, which can create credentials that survive password resets.

Microsoft rates it Moderate (CVSS 6.5), but CISA has already added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Organisations that prioritise by CVSS alone will miss it.

The Preview Pane is not affected, so the victim has to open the file. Microsoft shipped fixes on November 10 in an Office update, not a Windows update.

Affected Office builds, exploit mechanics, detection queries and mitigation steps: https://thecybersecguru.com/news/cve-2026-124194-outlook-ntlm-zero-day/

CVE-2026-98432.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv4: free inet_opt and ireq_opt after an RCU grace period

tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() transfers ownership of ireq->ireq_opt to the
child socket (newinet->inet_opt) without copying it.

Another cpu can concurrently process a retransmitted SYN for the same
request socket, and send a SYNACK from tcp_check_req().
tcp_v4_send_synack() and inet_csk_route_req() read ireq->ireq_opt
under rcu_read_lock() only, and ip_build_and_send_pkt() and
ip_options_build() then read opt->optlen twice.

Note that the SYNACK timer itself is not an issue: it holds a
reference on its request socket, and inet_csk_reqsk_queue_drop()
calls timer_delete_sync() before the child can be freed.

Since commit 079096f103fa ("tcp/dccp: install syn_recv requests
into ehash table"), request sockets are processed without holding
the listener lock, so nothing prevents the child socket from being
freed while the SYNACK is still being built. TCP child sockets do
not have SOCK_RCU_FREE, and inet_sock_destruct() frees inet_opt
with a plain kfree(), leading to a use-after-free in
ip_options_build().

A similar issue exists with request socket migration
(net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req=1, or a BPF_SK_REUSEPORT_SELECT_OR_MIGRATE
program). reqsk_timer_handler() clones the request socket with
inet_reqsk_clone(), so that the old request socket and its clone
share the same ireq_opt, then reqsk_migrate_reset() clears the
pointer in the old one. Another cpu holding a reference on the old
request socket can still be using these options (sending a SYNACK,
or creating a child in tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock()) when the clone is
freed, and tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor() also uses a plain kfree().

Readers already use RCU, and other paths replacing inet_opt
(do_ip_setsockopt(), cipso_v4_sock_setattr()...) already use
kfree_rcu(). Use kfree_rcu() in inet_sock_destruct() and
tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor() as well.

IPv6 is not affected by the first issue, because tcp_v6_syn_recv_sock()
duplicates the options. tcp_v6_reqsk_destructor() has the same
migration issue with ipv6_opt, which is only set by CALIPSO. This
will be addressed in a separate patch.

CVE-2026-109518.description:
On Debian, Ubuntu, and derivative Linux distributions, an on-path attacker who can manipulate the HTTP traffic (including a malicious mirror or proxy) between an APT client and an archive server triggered by a package install can trick the client into installing an attacker-controlled unverified package and achieve remote code execution with root privileges.



The vulnerability is caused by the reuse of hard links and requires the client to follow redirects and retry the download of package files. It requires the client to have a non-zero Acquire::Retries configuration setting; the value 3 is the default starting with Debian 12 (bookworm) and Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (Jammy Jellyfish), so older releases are unaffected in a default configuration

posts.content:
This doesn't mean CVSS is a good system for CVE scoring. I don't think it is, at least not with significant extra effort on the side of software providers and vulnerability management teams.

To quote the CVSS 4 specs:

CVSS Base Score (CVSS-B) Measures Severity, not Risk.

This is critical & to be frank, I very much dislike CVSS-BTE, I still would absolutely not build a VM program on top of it, even knowing it exists & should be used instead of raw -B. I personally also think that attack complexity is still less impactful than it should be in even CVSS 4, but that's my heretical take, I guess. But even its own specs call this out.

The other critical part I'd like to quote is this:

3.10: Multiple CVSS Base (CVSS-B) Scores
It is common for a vulnerability to be present on multiple product versions, platforms, and/or operating systems. In some circumstances, the Base metrics may differ on different product versions, platforms, and/or operating systems. For example, a hypothetical vulnerability is applicable to multiple operating systems produced by the same vendor. The Attack Complexity (AC) of this vulnerability on a legacy operating system is Low (L). However, a newer operating system has new inherent protection capabilities that change the Attack Complexity to High (H). This variance ultimately leads to different CVSS-B scores for the same vulnerability on the two operating systems.
It is acceptable to assess and publish multiple CVSS-B scores for a single vulnerability provided each has additional language outlining the specific product versions, platforms, and/or operating systems that are relevant to each CVSS-B score. Values for all CVSS-B metrics (not only a numeric CVSS-B score) must be supplied for each affected product version, platform, and/or operating system using a standard format. In situations where multiple CVSS-B scores are applicable but only one is provided, the highest CVSS-B score must be utilized.

This is fortunately something where we have been seeing positive developments from Linux distros over the last years, with individual advisories, individual scores, and OS-specific mitigations. This is a solid foundation we can use for building a vulnerability management, even on CVSS.

This also brings me to what imo is one of the more questionable CISA KEV entries: CVE-2026-111497 (Brotli). Prioritizing based on KEV lists is great because its an efficient way to eliminate the truly critical vulnerabilities. It may be that I am simply not privy to the super secret CISA infos but adding the library vulnerability without specifically attacked targets to the catalogue somewhat undermines this.

CVE-2026-104007.description: LibreOffice can connect to databases through JDBC drivers written in Java. A spreadsheet can use a database as the source of a pivot table, and the database document that describes the connection names the driver to use. The location the driver was loaded from was taken from the database document itself, so a crafted document could make LibreOffice load and run Java code that the document supplied when it was opened. This is a different route to the problem fixed for CVE-2026-63277. In fixed versions the driver location is taken only from the driver configuration of the user, and a pivot table whose source is a database document named by a URL connects only once the user allows links to be updated.

HSQLDB lets SQL statements call Java methods, limited to the classes that are permitted. When HSQLDB was used through the generic JDBC driver this limit did not apply, so SQL in a crafted document could call any Java method and run code. In fixed versions SQL can call only the built-in functions of HSQLDB, whichever way the database is reached.

PostgreSQL just patched 52 security vulnerabilities, including a 22-year-old bug that can lead to remote code execution.

The most alarming finding: CVE-2026-6460. A type confusion flaw dating back to May 2004 allowed stale composite-type values to be interpreted using the wrong memory layout. A researcher demonstrated how to turn this into code execution as the PostgreSQL server's OS user.

32 vulnerabilities carry CVSS 8.8.

Managed PostgreSQL services are affected too.
C-language extensions must be rebuilt for full protection.

This is not just another database patch. It changes the extension ABI, requires index rebuilding, and makes existing incremental backups untrustworthy.

A 22-year-old bug. 52 CVEs. One release that database administrators cannot afford to treat as routine maintenance.

CVE-2026-53998.description: Phoenix is an AI observability and evaluation platform. From 13.0.0 until 15.7.0, the applyChatTemplate GraphQL query passed attacker-controlled F-string templates to FStringTemplateFormatter._format, while DotDict.__getattr__ did not prevent traversal through Python private attributes. A crafted field could traverse object internals such as __class__, __init__, and __globals__ to read process environment variables and internal module state. The endpoint is unauthenticated on default installations, and any account can reach it when authentication is enabled. Exposure of PHOENIX_SECRET can allow administrative session-token forgery and decryption of credentials protected by keys derived from that secret. This issue is fixed in version 15.7.0.

posts.content:
🚨 A simple unauthenticated MongoDB ping could poison a replica set and crash its next primary during failover.

CVE-2026-118383 carries a CVSS 9.5 and exposes a dangerous pre-authentication use-after-free vulnerability affecting MongoDB replica set members.
The attack is particularly nasty because it does not require database credentials.

An attacker sends just TWO crafted ping commands containing readConcern.afterOpTime, planting persistent notification objects inside MongoDB's replication bookkeeping. The commands time out. The attacker disconnects. Everything appears normal.
Then, potentially hours or days later, the poisoned member wins a replica set election while lagging behind another member. A double teardown frees a CatchupState object while it is still executing, potentially crashing the newly elected primary before it accepts a single write.

The demonstrated impact is denial of service. Arbitrary code execution is theoretically possible but has NOT been demonstrated.

Affected deployments include MongoDB replica set members across multiple release branches. Standalone mongod instances and mongos routers are not affected.

Fixed versions:
• 9.0.7
• 8.3.16
• 8.0.37
• 7.0.48
• 6.0.30
• 5.0.35
• 4.4.32

Full technical breakdown, root cause, attack sequence, detection rules and patching guidance:
https://thecybersecguru.com/news/mongodb-cve-2026-118383-use-after-free/

#MongoDB #CyberSecurity #InfoSec #CVE2026118383 #DatabaseSecurity #ZeroDay #VulnerabilityResearch #DevSecOps

CVE-2026-118383.description: A use-after-free in the replication component of MongoDB Server can occur when a newly elected replica set primary completes catch-up. The condition can be caused by requests that do not require authentication, and may result in the server terminating unexpectedly or, under certain conditions, arbitrary code execution in the context of the server process. Replica set members are affected, including the shard and config server replica set members of sharded clusters; standalone mongod instances are not.
